correctness.rationale: The theorem partitions all possible 5-good 3-block partitions into (3,1,1) and (2,2,1), handles coincident singleton cases by an explicit disjoint choice, other configurations by Hall plus complementary triple, and identifies the only obstruction using the 3 perfect matchings of K4. There are exactly 5*3!=30 obstructions among Stirling S(5,3)^3=25^3 ordered triples, one relabeling orbit. For any normalized monotone valuations with 3 agents and 5 goods, MMS partitions can be chosen nonempty (also if MMS is zero); a disjoint block transversal is sufficient for an MMS allocation. The canonical monotone binary witness has MMS 1 for each agent and no fair allocation. A self-contained checker independently enumerates all 15625 triples, checks the predicted pattern, orbit and 243 allocations. Analytical proof handles the universal valuation quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The closest primary source Feige (arXiv:2610.06125, 2026-10-05) already supplies a general monotone-MMS nonexistence construction, including the three-agent five-good example. What is claimed here is exclusively the reverse direction and unique structural classification of all failing triples of five-good partitions, their exact cardinality 30 among 25^3, and one relabeling orbit. These are not logical corollaries merely of the existence construction, and no such classification was found in materially inspected relevant sections and appendix. A mathematically identical unindexed or uninspected combinatorial lemma remains a publication-priority risk.
residual_risks: A combinatorics/rainbow-matching classification outside the inspected MMS literature may be equivalent or stronger.
The abstract-only additive reference does not exclude all small-case remarks in its full text.
The finite checker establishes a complete census only for 3 partitions on 5 labeled elements, not an independent audit of the unrestricted set-function claim.

value.rationale: Rather than recomputing a known existence bound, the result isolates a unique natural forbidden configuration of fair-allocation partitions at the first three-agent monotone-MMS failure size. It gives both a complete structurally interpretable classification and exact count, enabling conditional positive results for restricted valuations that cannot realize the obstruction. Its minimality and unavoidable structure make it a useful building block, not an arbitrary small numerical slice.
